states.findings: Quiet breathing/posture changes and one readable closed-eye blink return to open eyes. Silhouette and foot base remain stable; neutral reference was also inspected.

Right-facing gait shows extended and gathered leg phases with countering arms. Anatomical-left headset is far-side/occluded; no mirrored near-ear duplicate is visible. Limbs and boots stay inside the cell.

Distinct left-facing gait shows alternating extension/gather phases. Single anatomical-left headset remains visible on the near ear throughout; character design and body scale match the opposite gait.
Neutral hands progress to raised open palm, a changed wave angle and lowered return. Headset remains on the opposite, anatomical-left ear and the head does not drift.

Crouch, ascent, joyful arms-up apex, descent and low landing/settle are all visible in order. Height changes come from pose and vertical motion; head identity is stable and neither hands nor boots are clipped. Final settle is a low landing pose.
Hands gather, eyelids and head lower into disappointment, then posture and eyes recover to an open neutral endpoint. No facial identity change or permanent collapsed pose.

Open palms, expectant head tilt, offered hands and briefly clasped hands create a readable awaiting-response gesture, ending back at open palms. Cream/mint sleeves and hands remain intact on both backgrounds.

Stationary activity/thinking action raises the anatomical-left hand to the left-ear headset, closes eyes in concentration, lowers the hand and returns. It is visually distinct from the directional gait actions.
Hands held behind, mild left/right head/eye scan, slight lean and downward nod return to front. The motion remains restrained and uses the same face, bob and headset.

All four cardinals and quadrant progression read correctly in clockwise order. Body/base and single-ear headset semantics are consistent. Weak157.5/337.5 horizontal cues and similar292.5/315 poses are documented in direction-semantics.json.
